id: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十四-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十四
Maro's words made me think of religion.
u.src: 马咯的话让我联想到了宗教。

en: I was undoubtedly a firm materialist, and had never seriously considered religious questions.
u.src: 我无疑是个坚定的唯物主义者，从未严肃认真的考虑过宗教问题。

en: At that moment, moved by Tokka's death, I began to wonder what religion among the kappas really was.
u.src: 此时我被托喀的死触动，就开始思考河童的宗教究竟是什么。

en: I immediately asked the student Rapu.
u.src: 我当时马上问学生拉卟、。

en: We believe in Christianity, Buddhism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, and the like.
u.src: “我们信仰基督教、佛教、伊斯兰教、拜火教什么的。

en: The most powerful of them is the modern faith.
u.src: 势力最大的要数近代教了。

en: It is also called the religion of life.
u.src: 也叫生活教。”

en: The translation of the term "religion of life" may not be quite apt.
u.src: （“生活教”这个词的翻译可能不够贴切。

en: In the original, the word is Quemoocha.
u.src: 原文是Quemoocha。

en: The cha probably corresponds to the English suffix ism.
u.src: cha大概相当于英语中的ism 。

en: The original form of Quemoo, Quemal, does not mean only "life"; it also includes the sense of food, drink, and sexual relations.
u.src: Quemoo的原形Quemal不单指“生活”，还包括“饮食男女”的意思。）

en: So this country has churches and temples too?
u.src: “如此说来这个国家也有教会、寺院喽？”
“当然。

en: The great temple of the modern religion is the largest building in our country.
u.src: 近代教的大寺院是本国第一大建筑哩。

en: How about I take you to have a look?
u.src: 带你去参观一下，如何？”

en: On a warm afternoon, with the sky a little overcast, Lap proudly took me along to visit this great temple.
u.src: 一个温暖的下午，天气略阴沉，拉卟得意的陪我一起去参观这座大寺院了。

en: Sure enough, it was a majestic building at least ten times larger than the Nikolai Cathedral, and it combined nearly every architectural style.
u.src: 果不其然，这是一座至少比尼古莱教堂大十倍的巍峨雄壮的建筑物，并且融合了几乎所有的建筑样式。

en: Standing before the great temple and looking up at its towering spires and round domes, I unexpectedly felt a little afraid.
u.src: 我站在这座大寺院前面，望着那高耸的塔和圆屋顶时，竟然感到有些恐惧。

en: To tell the truth, they really looked very much like countless feelers reaching toward the sky.
u.src: 说真的，它们真的非常像是无数只伸向天空的触角。

en: We stood at the great gate, where we seemed even smaller beside it, and for a while looked up at this rare great temple of the world—
u.src: 我们在大门口站立（和这大门相比，我们愈加渺小了！），仰望了片刻这座世上少有的大寺院——

en: It was less a building than a colossal creature.
u.src: 与其说是建筑，不如说它是庞然大物。

en: The interior of the great temple was quite spacious.
u.src: 大寺院的内部好相当宽敞。

en: Several worshippers passed between the Corinthian-style columns.
u.src: 科林斯式风格的圆柱建筑之间有几个朝拜者穿行而过。

en: They, like us, looked extremely small.
u.src: 他们和我们一般，显得十分渺小。

en: Later, we also encountered an old, bent-backed kappa.
u.src: 后来我们还遇见一只弯腰驼背的老河童。

en: Rapp bowed his head to him in greeting and said with the deepest respect,
“Elder, it is truly wonderful that you are still so hale and strong.”
u.src: 拉卟对他低头致意，无比尊敬的说：“长老，您身体股如此硬朗，真是太棒啦。”

en: The old kappa bowed back as well and replied politely, "Is that you, Mr. Lapp?
u.src: 那只老河童也回了个礼，礼貌的回复说：“是拉卟先生吗？
你也……

en: (He stopped there, probably because he had only just noticed that Lapp's mouth was ulcerated.)
u.src: （他说到这停了下来，可能是因为才发现拉卟的嘴烂了。）
唔，你看来挺不错的。
你今天怎么……”

en: I came here today accompanying this gentleman.
u.src: “今天是陪这位先生一起来的。

en: You probably understand already, this gentleman...
u.src: 你大概也了解，这位先生……”

en: Rapp then began introducing my circumstances without stopping.
u.src: 拉卟接着开始不停的介绍我的情况。

en: It was as though he were making excuses for seldom coming to this great temple.
u.src: 像是为自己很少来这个大寺院来辩解。

ja: をしていただきたいのです
en: I would like to ask you to serve as this gentleman's guide.
u.src: “我希望邀请您给这位先生做向导。”

en: The elder smiled kindly and first exchanged greetings with us,
u.src: 长老亲切的微笑，首先跟我们寒暄了一下，

en: then quietly pointed toward the altar in front of us:
u.src: 接着静静的指了指正面的祭台：

ja: してあげられることは
en: There is truly nothing I can do for this gentleman.
u.src: “我真没什么为这位先生可效劳的。

en: What stands on the altar in front is the Tree of Life,
u.src: 正面祭台上的是‘生命之树’,

en: and we believers bow down before it in worship.
u.src: 我们信徒们会对它顶礼膜拜。
你也看到了，

en: golden and green fruits grow on the Tree of Life.
u.src: ‘生命之树’上长着金色和绿色的果实。

en: The golden fruit is called the fruit of good,
u.src: 金色的果实被称作‘善果’，

en: and the green one is called the fruit of evil..."
u.src: 绿色的被称作‘恶果’……”

en: Before long, the elder's explanation began to bore me.
u.src: 很快，长老的解说就让我觉得厌烦了。

en: Because of the extra explanation he had deliberately added, it sounded to me like a worn-out metaphor.
u.src: 因为他特别加上的说明，我听着却像是陈旧的比喻。

en: While pretending to listen attentively, I was secretly observing the inside of the great temple for myself.
u.src: 我一面假装认真地听着，一面自己偷偷观察大寺院内部。

en: Corinthian-style pillars, Gothic-style vaults, Arabian-style lattice patterns, and Secessionist prayer desks—
u.src: 科林斯式风格的柱子，哥特式风格的穹隆，阿拉伯风格的方格花纹，分离派的祈祷桌子——

en: All these things blended together harmoniously, and somehow they had a strange, wild, rough beauty.
u.src: 这些东西和谐的调和在一起，竟然有一种神奇的野性粗狂的美。

en: The marble busts in the niches on both sides especially drew my eye.
u.src: 两侧神龛里的大理石半身像尤其吸引我的目光。

en: I felt as though I had seen those statues before, which was not particularly strange.
u.src: 我对这些像似曾相似，这倒也不算神奇。

en: After the bent-backed old kappa finished his explanation of the Tree of Life, he accompanied Lap and me toward the niche on the right,
u.src: 那只弯腰驼背的老河童结束了“生命之树”的介绍后，陪着我和拉卟一起走向右边的神龛，

en: and described the bust inside the niche like this: "This is one of our saints, the saint Strindberg, who betrayed everything.
u.src: 他这样描述神龛里的半身像：“这是我们其中一个圣徒——背叛一切的圣徒斯特林堡。

en: It is said that after enduring every hardship, this saint was saved by Swedenborg's philosophy.
u.src: 据说这位圣徒历尽艰苦后被斯维登堡的哲学所解救。

en: But in fact, he was not saved at all.
u.src: 不过事实上他并没有得到解救。

en: This saint, like us, also believed in the Religion of Life; more precisely, believing in the Religion of Life was his only way out.
u.src: 这位圣徒也和我们一样信仰生活教——准确来说，他只有信仰生活教这一条出路。

en: Please read the book Legends, which this saint left to us.
u.src: 请读一下这位圣徒给我们留下的《传说》这本书。

en: He himself admits that he was a failed suicide."
u.src: 他自己承认，他是个自杀未遂者。”

en: As I looked at the second shrine, I began to feel somewhat depressed.
u.src: 看着第二个神龛，我有些郁闷起来。

en: It was the bust of a German man with a large beard.
u.src: 那是一座留着大胡子的德国人的半身像。

ja: 「これは『ツァラトゥストラ』の
en: This is Nietzsche, the famous poet and author of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.
u.src: “这是《扎拉图斯特拉》的作者——著名的诗人尼采。

en: This saint sought deliverance from the superman he himself had created.
u.src: 这位圣徒向他自己创造的超人寻求解脱。

en: But he could not attain deliverance; instead, he became a madman.
u.src: 但他没能获得解脱，反而成了疯子。

ja: にさえなれなかったかもしれない……」
en: If he had not gone mad, perhaps he could never even have become a saint...
u.src: 如果不是发疯了，没准他还成不了圣徒呢……”

en: The elder was silent for a while, then led me to the front of the third shrine.
u.src: 长老静默了片刻，接着就把我带到第三座神龛跟前。

en: In the third shrine was enshrined a bust of Tolstoy.
u.src: “第三座神龛里供的是托尔斯泰的半身像。

en: This saint's ascetic practice was harder than anyone else's.
u.src: 这位圣徒的修行比其他人都艰苦。

en: He had originally been an aristocrat, and did not want the curious public to see his suffering.
u.src: 他原来是个贵族，不希望被满是好奇心的公众看到自己的痛苦。

en: This saint struggled to believe in a Christ whom, in truth, he could not believe in,
u.src: 这位圣徒努力去信仰实际上并不能相信的基督，

en: and at one time he publicly declared that he held fast to his faith with absolute conviction.
u.src: 他曾经一度公开宣称他无比坚持自己的信仰。

en: In his later years, he finally could no longer endure being a tragic liar.
u.src: 直到晚年，他终于不堪忍受做一个悲壮撒谎者了。

en: It is very well known that he was often afraid of the beams in his study.
u.src: 他常常对书斋的房梁感到恐惧，这件事是非常有名的。

en: But he never chose suicide; otherwise, he could not have become a saint.
u.src: 不过他不曾选择自杀，否则他就成不了圣徒了。”

en: The bust enshrined in the fourth shrine was a Japanese person.
u.src: 第四座神龛里供的半身像是一个日本人。

en: When I saw this Japanese person, I felt a deep sense of warmth and familiarity.
u.src: 看见这个日本人的时候，我感到十分亲切。

en: This is the poet Kunikida Doppo, who deeply sympathized with the feelings of laborers who committed suicide by lying on the railway tracks.
u.src: “这是诗人国木田独步，他对卧轨自杀的体力劳动者的心情感同身受。

en: I suppose there is no need for me to introduce him to you.
u.src: 不用我跟你介绍了吧。

en: Next, please look at the fifth shrine..."
u.src: 下面一请看第五个神龛……”
“这不是瓦格纳吗？”
“是的。

en: Wagner was a friend of the king, and also a revolutionary.
u.src: 瓦格纳是国王的朋友，也是一位革命家。

en: In his later years, Saint Wagner even prayed before meals.
u.src: 晚年的圣徒瓦格纳，吃饭之前还要进行祈祷呢。

en: Without doubt, his faith in the religion of life far exceeded his faith in Christianity.
u.src: 无疑，他对生活教的信仰，远远超过了对基督教的信仰。

en: Judging from the letters he left behind,
u.src: 从他遗留下的书简来看，

en: while he was in this mortal world, illness and suffering nearly made him see death ahead of time on several occasions.
u.src: 他在凡间的时候数次被疾苦害的险些让他提前看见死神呢。”

en: By then, we were already standing before the sixth shrine.
u.src: 此时我们已经站在第六座神龛前了。

en: This is a friend of Saint Strindberg.
u.src: “这是圣徒斯特林堡的朋友。

en: He came from a French merchant family and was a French painter,
u.src: 他出身于法国的商人世家，是一个法国画家，

en: abandoned his lawful wife, who had borne him a large brood of children,
u.src: 抛弃了生了一大群孩子的原配，

en: and then married a girl named Guiti, only thirteen or fourteen years old.
u.src: 再娶了一个十三四岁的圭蒂姑娘。

en: This saint has thick blood vessels, and the blood of a sailor flows inside them.
u.src: 这位圣徒的血管很粗，里面流淌着水手的血液。

en: And look at those lips of his; they bear traces of something like arsenic.
u.src: 再看他那嘴唇，上面留着砒霜什么的之类的痕迹哩。
第七个神龛里的是……

en: Are you getting a little tired?
u.src: 你是不是有些累了。

en: Then please come this way with me.
u.src: 那么，请随我来这边来。”

en: I was truly somewhat tired, so I followed the elder with Rapp down a corridor filled with fragrance and into a room.
u.src: 我真的有些累了，于是就和拉卟一起跟随长老沿着弥漫着馨香的走廊进入一个房间。

en: In the corner of the room stood a black statue of the goddess Venus, and before it a bunch of wild grapes had been offered.
u.src: 房间角落里，有一座黑色的维纳斯女神塑像，塑像面供奉着一束野葡萄。

en: I had originally thought that a monk's cell would have no decorations, so I found this somewhat unexpected.
u.src: 我原先认为想僧房不会有什么装饰，所以对此有些意外。

en: The elder probably read my feelings from my expression, and before I had even sat down, he said apologetically:
u.src: 长老可能是从我神态看出了我的心情，在我没落座之前，就抱歉地说道：

en: Please do not forget that our faith is the religion of life.
u.src: “请不要忘记我们的信仰是生活教。

ja: きていくこと」なのです。
en: The doctrine of our god, the Tree of Life, is to live on full of vitality.
u.src: 我们的神——‘生命之树’的教义是‘生机勃勃地活下去’。

ja: ませたことがありますか。」
en: ... Rapp, have you had this gentleman read our Bible?
u.src: ……拉卟君，你让这位先生读过我们的《圣经》了吗？”
“并没有。

en: To tell the truth, I have hardly read them myself either,
u.src: ……说真的，我自己也基本上没读过哩，

en: Rapp rubbed the hollow on the top of his head and answered plainly.
u.src: ”拉卟摸了摸头顶的凹坑，直接地回答说。

en: The elder smiled peacefully as usual, then went on, "Then you do not know.
u.src: 长老照旧安宁地微笑，接着说：“那你就不知道了。

en: Our god created the entire world in a single day.
u.src: 我们的神用一天的时间就创造了整个世界。

en: Although the Tree of Life was also a tree, there was nothing it could not do.
u.src: （“生命之树”尽管也是一棵树，但是它却没有什么不能做到的事情。）

en: and then created the female kappa.
u.src: ，接着创造了雌河童。

en: But the female kappa was far too lonely by herself, and she needed a male kappa for company.
u.src: 但是只有雌河童太孤独了，它需要个雄河童来做伴。

en: Our god, moved by compassion, took out the female kappa's brain matter and created the male kappa.
u.src: 我们的神以慈悲为怀，取出雌河童的脑髓创造了雄河童。

en: Our god blessed this pair of kappa, saying, 'Eat, and live on with gusto.'"
u.src: 我们的神对这一对河童祝福着：‘吃吧，兴致勃勃地活下去。’”

en: The elder's words reminded me of the dead poet Tock.
u.src: 长老的话让我想起了死去的诗人托喀。

en: Unfortunately, he was an atheist just like me.
u.src: 不幸的是他和我一样是个无神论者。

en: Since I am not a kappa, it was understandable that I did not know the Religion of Life.
u.src: 我不是河童，不了解生活教也可以理解了。

en: But Tock, who lived in the land of the kappa, ought to have understood the true meaning of the Tree of Life.
u.src: 可是生活在河童国的托喀应该了解“生命之树”的真谛才对。

en: I pitied Tock because he had refused to follow the guidance of this truth, and so had come to such an end.
u.src: 我同情托喀不听这个真谛的指引，所以才有了这么一个结局。

en: So I interrupted the elder and told him about Tock.
u.src: 因此我打断长老的话，跟他讲述托喀的事。

en: After the elder had finished listening, he let out a deep sigh and said:
u.src: 长老听完之后，长叹了一口气说：
“哦，那个可怜的诗人……

en: The only things that decide our fate are faith, circumstances, and chance.
u.src: 决定我们命运的只有信仰、遭遇和机遇。

en: You may also want to add factors such as heredity, perhaps.
u.src: （可能你们还要加上遗传等因素吧。）

en: Tokku's greatest misfortune is that he has no faith.
u.src: 托喀君最大不幸的是没有信仰。”

ja: うらやましいのだろう。
en: Tock must envy you very much.
u.src: “托喀很羡慕你吧。

en: No, I envy you very much too, Rappu-kun; you are in the prime of youth...
u.src: 不，我也非常羡慕你，拉卟君风华正茂……”
我说。

ja: でいられたかもしれませんね。
en: If my mouth had not rotted, I might have been a little more optimistic.
u.src: “我的嘴要是没烂，可能我会乐观一点呢。”
拉卟也插话说。

en: After listening to us finish speaking, the elder let out another long sigh.
u.src: 听我们说完，长老又长长地叹了一口气。

en: His eyes were full of tears as he stared fixedly at the black statue of Venus.
u.src: 他满目含泪，直勾勾地盯着那尊黑色的维纳斯像。

en: Actually, I too... this is a secret, and you must not tell anyone...
u.src: “其实我也……这是一个秘密，你不能跟任何人说……

en: The truth is, I do not believe in our god either.
u.src: 事实上我也不信仰我们的神。

en: But sooner or later, someday, my prayers...
u.src: 但是迟早有一天，我的祈祷……”

en: Before the elder could finish speaking, the door suddenly opened, and a strong female kappa lunged fiercely at him.
u.src: 长老话没说完，突然房门被打开了，一只健壮的雌河童向他猛地扑了过来。

ja: めようとするどころか、
en: Before we could even try to stop her, the female kappa knocked the elder down to the ground in a flash.
u.src: 别说我们想拦住她，但是电光火石之间这只雌河童就把长老扑倒在地。
“死老头子！

en: You stole money from my wallet today; did you take it to go drinking again?
u.src: 今天你从我的皮夹子偷走了钱，是不是又拿去喝酒了！”

en: After a little more than ten minutes, we left the elder and his wife behind and rushed out through the main gate of the great temple as if we were fleeing.
u.src: 过了十来分钟，我们将长老夫妇留在后面，逃跑一样奔出了大寺院的正门。

en: After we had walked quietly for a while, Lapp said to me, "Judging from what we just saw, the elder probably doesn't believe in the 'Tree of Life' either."
u.src: 我们静静地走了一阵之后，拉卟跟我说：“看刚才那副情景，长老也就不会信仰‘生命之树’啦。”

en: I did not answer, but I could not help turning my head to look at the great temple.
u.src: 我没有回复，却不禁扭头看了看大寺院。

en: The great temple's towering spires and round domes reached toward the gloomy sky like countless feelers,
u.src: 大寺院那高耸的塔和圆屋顶像无数的触角般地伸向阴郁的天空，

en: and a fearful atmosphere hung all around, no different from a mirage appearing in the desert sky...
u.src: 周围弥漫着一种恐怖的气氛，和出现在沙漠的天空上的海市蜃楼并无二致……
